result.title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
result.summary: Private, personalised language models must run on local consumer devices, where large, frontier models cannot fit, and retaining long contexts is non-trivial. Sequential memory---the key-value (KV) cache---grows linearly with context length, quickly dwarfing the model itself: for Qwen3-1.7B-Base, 200,000 retained entries require 21 GiB, 6.6 times more than the model weights. Yet the KV-cache compression methods we measured fail beyond moderate compression ratios. We introduce Transformer-FSQ, addressing extreme KV-cache compression by replacing standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation bottleneck. Our cache stores a packed vector of discrete integer codes per token, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer trains only these projections on 0.25 tokens per original parameter. We evaluate Transformer-FSQ against five baseline families on models from 0.6B to 8B parameters. On long-context retrieval (RULER), from 12$\times$ to 97.5$\times$ Transformer-FSQ is the most accurate method we evaluate, across scales. A fused Triton kernel decodes directly from the integer codes; with baselines given their authors' kernels where available, it decodes at $1.01\times$ (95% interval $0.98$--$1.05$) the throughput of native SDPA attention on the uncompressed Qwen3-8B-Base at $32\times$ and $1.54\times$ at $97.5\times$. Extreme KV-cache compression is therefore a practical way to extend how much context a fixed device can hold.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Transformer-FSQ，用有限标量量化瓶颈替换标准 K/V 投影，使 KV cache 以每 token 的离散整数码存储且无需逐 token 量化元数据，并在 0.6B–8B 模型上以长上下文检索（RULER）和解码吞吐评估极端压缩比下的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 对缓存状态的极端离散压缩可能决定视觉细节等任务必要信息能否保留在内部状态中，其量化粒度与信息坍缩、下游可用性的关系可供核查；但该文为纯文本效率研究，未涉及多模态推理。
